newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Aug domestic oil export down 8.9pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Aug domestic oil export down 8.9pct.

text.p: Singapore's domestic oil exports in August dropped 8.9 percent to Singapore $1.211 billion over July, the Trade Development Board (TDB) said on Friday.
"The emergence of Thailand as a regional exporter and the expansion of refining capacities in South Korea have contributed to the weakness of Asian oil exports, including Singapore," the TDB said.
Domestic oil export growth moderated to 12.2 percent for the three-months average to August over the same period of the previous year.
The three-months average growth to July was 13.8 percent and for the months to June it was 22.5 percent.
Exports in July amounted to S$1.329 billion and in June to S$1.372 billion.

The fall in exports coincided with a reduction in refinery runs in Singapore during July and August due to poor margins. Output was also reduced by the shutdown of Shell Singapore's 200,000 barrels-per-day for a month-long maintenance in early August.
